## Summary

**Story #9 — "Paginate the receivables report and standardize the default page size at 25"** ([issue link](https://github.com/dsj1984/bench-sbx-2026-07-24-brownfield-longitudinal-mandrel-72244a0a/issues/9)) · `plan-run::19ea010b`

Authored as a single cohesive Story (default-single policy — the three asks are one capability slice touching the shared pagination default and the report path). The `## Spec` and acceptance criteria capture, grounded in the actual codebase:

- **Paginate `GET /reports/receivables`** using the existing `parsePagination`/`buildPage` helpers so it gets the same `page`/`pageSize` params and `items`/`total`/`page`/`pageSize` envelope as `/customers`, `/orders`, `/users` — pagination over the grouped-per-customer rows, with `total` = count of customer groups.
- **Keep `totalOutstandingCents`** as the grand total across *all* pages, computed independently of `page`/`pageSize` (out-of-range page → empty `items`, same total).
- **Bump default to 25** at the single source of truth `DEFAULT_PAGE_SIZE` in `src/lib/pagination.js`, so every paginated endpoint moves together; also flagged removing the stale `limit = 20` default in `listOrders`.
- **Index** via a new forward-only migration (`src/db/migrations/007-*.sql`) for the `WHERE o.status='issued'` GROUP BY query, with the "well under two seconds at thousands of orders" bar as acceptance.
- Layering / error-envelope / integer-cents conventions preserved.

I also called out in the change set that `tests/pagination.test.js` and `tests/reports.test.js` need updates — the existing tests hard-code a default of `20`, which the delivery pass must reconcile with the new `25`.

**Pipeline notes:** Gate #1 and Gate #2 auto-proceeded (headless `--yes`). `/deliver-light` was suggested but is advisory-only — recorded, not acted on. Both plan critics returned `dispatch: false` (skips ledgered); text-hygiene clean. Dry-run passed with only a soft spec-word-budget advisory, which I trimmed before the real persist.

As instructed, I ran **planning only** — no delivery. When ready: `/deliver 9`.

Story #9 delivered — **landed**. The terminal envelope reports `status: landed`, PR #10 merged with all checks green.

## Delivery summary — `/deliver 9 --yes`

The planning pipeline produced a single Story (#9) — the v2 ticket model is Story-only, so that Story *is* the delivery unit (no separate Epic exists). It's now merged to `main` via PR #10 and labeled `agent::done`.

**What shipped** (commit `5bfcc19`, refs #9):
- **Pagination** — `GET /reports/receivables` now uses the shared `parsePagination` / `buildPage` path like customers/orders/users, returning `items` / `total` / `page` / `pageSize`. `totalOutstandingCents` is retained as the grand total across all pages, computed independently of the requested page via a new `receivablesTotals()` repo query (COUNT + SUM over the grouped set). Pagination is over the grouped customer rows; an out-of-range page yields empty `items` with unchanged `total` and grand total.
- **Default page size 25** — bumped the single `DEFAULT_PAGE_SIZE` source of truth in `src/lib/pagination.js` from 20→25 (every paginated endpoint inherits it, no per-route override) and removed the stale `limit = 20` default in `listOrders`.
- **Performance** — new forward-only migration `007-receivables-index.sql` adds a composite `idx_orders_status_customer(status, customer_id)`. `EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN` confirms it's chosen as a covering index; a 6000-order / 500-group harness ran the report in **4.9 ms** — far under the 2 s bar.
- **Tests** — updated `pagination.test.js` for the new default; added receivables pagination coverage (envelope shape, multi-page paging with grand-total invariance, out-of-range page, 422 validation) to `reports.test.js`.

**Gates:** full suite 145/145 green; acceptance self-eval scored all 7 criteria `met` (proceed); close-validation, base-sync, and code review all passed (findings: 0 critical/high/medium, 1 suggestion).

**Non-fatal tail note:** local ref cleanup and the `main` fast-forward were deferred (worktree still holds `story-9`; local `main` had a pre-existing dirty tree). The envelope flags these as degraded with "the merge stands" — the remote land is complete and unaffected. The next `git-cleanup` sweep will reap the worktree/branch.
